note_en: The English edition of the errata register. It is the same register: one summary per entry id, in the order the entries are published. The Chinese what/why/fix fields and every entry's commit join live in errata.json beside this file, which points here by path.

summaries.E01: Two machine-readable references pointed at feature ids that do not exist — `BUILDING-001` and `LANDUSE-001` against the real `BLDG-001` and `LU-001`.
summaries.E02: ”less than half the second-thinnest track” did not hold arithmetically: 14 against 28 is exactly half.
summaries.E03: Six of twelve scenario cards wrote the benchmark as `BM-2x` or `BM-3xx` — placeholders, not ids, joining to no point in the shipped geometry.
summaries.E04: The English card table silently dropped the spatial-anchor column while its own opening sentence declared that column mandatory.
summaries.E05: Three structural conclusions at the end of `verify.js` were `console.log` only and never reached the exit code — flip `official_boundary` to true and it printed the problem and passed.
summaries.E06: Two of three named constraints were referenced nowhere in the package, and the third was cited four times against the wrong feature.
summaries.E07: A class-1 metrics table still carried 82,413 m² while the same document, two hundred lines away, called that value superseded.
summaries.E08: 369.3 ha was attributed to a single feature that is 192.9 ha on its own; 369.3 is the total of three.
summaries.E09: The third phase layer contained 96.44% of the second, double-counting 40% of the area — the phasing expressed no sequence at all.
summaries.E10: A closing route self-intersected: the straight return to the origin crossed two of its own earlier legs, one of them within 6 m of a benchmark.
summaries.E11: Three benchmarks had no walkable connection to the spine — 501 m, 323 m and 59.8 m away — joined only by survey chords, in a proposal whose argument is that anyone can walk up to one.
summaries.E12: Three buildings stood on land uses that contradict their own type, the worst a 7,820 m² mobility hub sitting entirely inside park green space.
summaries.E13: `non_ai_path_available` was not required by the schema and the checker rejected only an explicit false — omitting the field passed, so the AI-off guarantee could be satisfied by silence.
summaries.E14: The census front-matter parser read inline arrays only and could not see YAML block lists, so four proposals' declared tracks were never counted by any run.
summaries.E15: ”Origin datum” was attached to the wrong benchmark: in surveying it is the point heights are transferred *from*, which here is BM-0, as the package's own closure checker already enforced.
summaries.E16: A closing route is checkable because it ends on a second independently known point, and the checker verified the start and never the end.
summaries.E17: The 412.5 m reading, cited eight times, could not be recomputed by a reviewer: the package shipped the derived scalar and not the coordinates, and the measuring script lived outside it.
summaries.E18: `sources.json` said the package no longer redistributes the source database. Shipping OSM coordinates made that false the moment it was done — an extracted subset is an ODbL derivative.
summaries.E19: The A3 cover overprinted its own contents, the disclaimer sat on another line, the frame rule ran between two rows and the last line fell outside the frame — while `overflow_qa` reported zero, because it compared text against the frame and this was text against text.
summaries.E20: Every A0 board was 38% blank: three sheets to a board are height-constrained, so each used 62% of the width available to it.
summaries.E21: The HTML report never parsed block quotes or bold, so the opening epigraph rendered as a run-on sentence with a literal `>` and 1,168 literal asterisks printed across the document.
summaries.E22: The offline page kept a third hand-copied set of scenario cards, still carrying placeholder benchmark ids the rest of the package had already fixed, and a drawing list frozen at nine sheets while twelve shipped.
summaries.E23: The manifest declared `data_confidence: medium` at the top level and `high` inside `validation_claim` — one file, two confidences.
summaries.E24: A metrics table headed “all class-1 values” listed seven of nine; two metrics were added to `metrics.json` and never to the hand-built table.
summaries.E25: A route legend still showed the closing tail that had been removed from the geometry two days earlier.
summaries.E26: A hierarchy table listed the origin among the first-order points while the legend four lines below, on the same sheet, distinguished them correctly.
summaries.E27: A land-use legend listed six classes against a seven-class partition, and the map silently drew the seventh through its unknown-code fallback as grey “other”.
summaries.E28: A sheet footer disclaimed a reading of 0.86 as illustrative while the plate drawn above it showed 0.26 — a caveat protecting a number that was not on the sheet.
summaries.E29: A sheet said PR numbers had passed 900 when they had passed 1,000, on a branch whose own PR was #1065.
summaries.E30: The manifest and the rights ledger both counted 80 files while the copyright statement said 77, and its own category table also totalled 77.
summaries.E31: The census-claims gate asked only whether the current value appeared somewhere, so it could not see the same quantity written as an older value elsewhere in the document.
summaries.E32: ”The matcher in #957 is an empty set on the historical corpus — 1,203 actions, 0 matches, so it will never fire”. All 1,203 came from an older prompt that never asked for the prefix being counted; measuring a token's rate in a corpus that never required it can only return zero.
summaries.E33: `overflow_qa` measured every run against the frame rule while its own error text said “footer rule” — the check and its message named different lines.
summaries.E34: A figure called land-use-structure contained no land-use structure: it drew the three scope levels and the benchmark orders instead.
summaries.E35: The list of files the reviewing model receives was read wrong in three ways, in the measurement built to establish what the reviewer actually sees.
summaries.E36: Four compliance-matrix references all resolved and all pointed at the wrong section — each to the chapter answering the *next* requirement. Resolution is not aim.
summaries.E37: The narrative opened with 228 proposals, 69 undisclosed, 84 strings, 9 model families, and the assumption register agreed — while the corpus had long since become 354 / 106 / 113 / 8.
summaries.E38: The sheet titled “three key areas and benchmark layout” drew the three key areas as three empty dashed boxes — one of the five figures the reviewer always receives, and the deliverable for the taskbook's detailed-design requirement.
summaries.E39: A new build step read the shipped *copy* of the field map while the step that refreshes that copy ran after it, so a census that had moved was reported from the stale one.
summaries.E40: Repeated reviews of one head SHA were treated as a repeatability measurement of the review instrument, when the queue's cache did not check model, endpoint or reasoning effort — so the repeat may have been the same answer served twice.
summaries.E41: A comment claimed seven font copies would collapse into one. Measured: fourteen embedded font programs and 10.54 MB of uncompressed glyph data, six distinct Regulars and six distinct Bolds.
summaries.E42: The land-use table listed six classes against a seven-class partition in the shipped geometry; the missing one was the station-concourse connection, in both languages at once.
summaries.E43: An eleven-column table's separator was written as eleven `|---|` cells run together, parsing to 21 fields against an 11-column header, so no renderer draws it as a table.
summaries.E44: A reference audit found anchors that resolve and point the wrong way — the referent exists and the direction is wrong, which no existence check can see.
summaries.E45: ”Across 351 proposals there is not one erratum” was measured once and then quoted from memory; re-measured it was false.
summaries.E46: ”The placeholder count held at 107 across the last four readings” — recovered from this branch's own history, one of those readings was 105, the run was three not four, and the numerator had fallen while the sentence claimed stability.
summaries.E47: Twenty-two of forty-four evidence summaries appended “independently recomputed by verify.js” to every metric they named, while that script recomputes only the seventeen marked class 1 — a file credited with work it declines to do.
summaries.E48: The front matter said twelve repeatable censuses had been run while the reading log held fourteen, and the body said fourteen twice.
summaries.E49: Two sources were graded `official_context` while both carried `source_type: agent_inferred_from_public_data` — the evidence class outranked the provenance it rested on.
summaries.E50: The wall built to display this network's own failures stood where the institution stands, about 3 km from the community point where inconsistent readings actually land. **Bad news belongs where it happened.**
summaries.E51: An eleven-column table declared a 21-field separator and stopped rendering as a table, directly beneath the sentence asserting every column was mandatory — in the English edition only.
summaries.E52: The sheet frame prints the other language's title opposite the figure number, and every string passes through the translator — so each English sheet printed its own English title twice and never the Chinese one.
summaries.E53: The type-width table used to lay out every drawing carried estimates of 0.52 em lowercase; measured against the actual font with fontTools it is 0.572, so every line had been laid out against a width the font does not have.
summaries.E54: `overflow_qa` kept its own copy of that width table. The previous erratum corrected the one in `figures.py` and not the one in the gate, so the gate judged overruns by the numbers the fix had just replaced.
summaries.E55: The cover truncated over-long titles to the column width — truncating the *Chinese* title, while English is substituted afterwards and runs about 80% longer, so “truncated” titles ran into the next column.
summaries.E56: The kit of parts had a column headed “the hard constraint a fabricator could fail” and not one entry carried a number: flush with no tolerance, seating with no height, guidance with no width. **The package contained no millimetre at all.**

split_note_en: The organisers cap a single JSON at 512 KiB. This file carries the most recent 320 English summaries and the other 56 are in visual/assets/errata.en-archive.json, same schema, nothing removed and no wording changed. Both state the total, so neither can be read as the whole. The Chinese register has been split this way since E307; this one was written whole until it crossed the cap (E377).
